status: PERMANENT REQUIREMENT — design proposals, not implemented enemies
scope: All 10 arcs / 100 missions; preserve existing completed missions
findings: Only Missions 1–10 are playable. Later arcs are campaign archive entries, not implemented encounters.
Five current enemy types share common combat infrastructure. Warrior and Heavy use the same soldier-source rig with scale/material/armor differences; this cannot satisfy later-arc uniqueness.
Expansion bosses share substantial model and phase infrastructure; decorative accents or speed changes alone cannot satisfy unique future bosses.
Future encounter data must be explicit. Do not use getEnemySpawns' current Mission 1 fallback as a future-arc roster.
rules: Each arc introduces a distinct faction identity, body/armor/clothing/helmet/face silhouettes, melee/ranged technology, behavior, roster and boss design. Recolors, scaled shared bodies and renamed attacks do not pass.
Reuse sensing, navigation, targeting, damage, telegraph and animation infrastructure where useful, while authoring different models, movesets and tactical decisions.
Preserve all current mission IDs, purposes, order, story decisions, rewards and saves. Faction names and boss concepts here are original proposals, not film canon or changes to established events.
The existing Arc 1 roster and victories remain intact. Its design entry documents its identity; no retroactive faction rewrite is authorized.

Later factions may serve the same established power without reusing its earlier troops. Arc 5 remains connected to the Complex assault; a new corps must not replace that story event with an unrelated antagonist.
Arcs 3 and 8 may involve multiple groups as their existing narrative requires; a distinctive primary faction does not erase existing multi-faction events.
Ashwatthama remains an important Arc 4 ally in Missions 31–40. Enemies threaten the sanctuary and evacuation; do not turn him into a disposable boss or resolve his oath prematurely.
A boss is not automatically assigned to every mission. Place encounters only where the existing mission purpose supports them, without changing mission completion or unlock rules prematurely.

arcDesigns.title: Kashi & the Bounty Hunter
arcDesigns.faction: Existing local bounty rivals, security forces and Glass Wastes defenders
arcDesigns.identity: Preserve the current varied Kashi opposition and named bosses; no new retroactive lore.
arcDesigns.design: Existing scavenged armor, local guards and crystalline silhouettes remain the reference baseline that future factions must differ from.

roster.elite: Existing encounter-specific veterans, retain current data
roster.ranged: Future local ranged unit only if separately authorized; current Scout is not a verified rifle class

boss.models: Preserve Warden, Prism Sovereign and existing expansion bosses
boss.mechanics: Preserve tested encounters; do not impose future faction mechanics retroactively

arcDesigns.animation: Preserve working clips; current shared soldier model remains an acknowledged art limitation.

arcDesigns.title: Complex & Yaskin
arcDesigns.faction: Custodial Directorate — proposed Complex logistics/security branch
arcDesigns.identity: Institutional extraction and access control; treats people and resources as inventory under the existing regime.
arcDesigns.design: Sealed porcelain shells, recessed asymmetric visors, tall narrow human operators and squat industrial chassis. No reused Kashi guard bodies.

roster.basic: Seal Warden: articulated shield cuff and short shock prod; locks passage in pairs
roster.elite: Audit Duelist: long split visor, precision energy lance; counters repeated frontal strikes
roster.heavy: Cargo Bastion: wide four-legged forklift chassis with hydraulic clamp; anchors a corridor
roster.ranged: Index Marksman: optic hood, braced coil projector; marks a line before a burst
roster.special: Relay Mote: floating ring sensor; links nearby shields until its exposed relay is interrupted

arcDesigns.combat: Deliberate formations, shield links and interlock defense; flank relays, interrupt setup and exploit recovery. No unavoidable full-corridor attacks.

boss.name: Intake Marshal
boss.model: Unique suspended central chassis with three folding manipulator arms and visible relay spine
phases: Sweep arms telegraph separate safe lanes
Freight anchors shield the chassis; disable reachable anchors
Detached arm pair changes spacing while the core exposes recovery windows
boss.counterplay: Interrupt relays and dodge committed sweeps; never reduce the fight to a recolored radial-slam boss

arcDesigns.animation: Mechanical clamp plants, shield interlock, braced recoil, armor-break stagger and staged chassis collapse; bespoke arm rig for boss.
arcDesigns.introduction: 11–13 teach wardens and line fire;14–16 introduce relay/duelist and freight heavy;17–19 combine known tools;20 may host the existing entry-conflict climax if its script supports it. Mission12's archived Prism entry is preserved pending review, not silently replaced.

arcDesigns.title: Sumathi & the Pursuit
arcDesigns.faction: Trailbound Compact — proposed pursuit-specialist bounty coalition
arcDesigns.identity: Competing trackers cooperating temporarily for a bounty; supports the existing multi-faction ambush and protection choices.
arcDesigns.design: Lean weathered trackers, open faces, layered wind wraps, low-profile scavenged harnesses and tall pack-carriers. Distinct from sealed Directorate uniforms.

roster.basic: Dust Runner: hooked short blade, crouched lateral rush and withdrawal
roster.elite: Twin-Trace Hunter: paired tether knives, feints then commits to a punishable attack
roster.heavy: Pack Ram: broad load-bearing suit and impact pole; charges only along a marked route
roster.ranged: Ridge Harrier: folding longbow-like rail launcher; relocates between marked shots
roster.special: Scent Weaver: spool backpack and visible tracking tags; lays disarmable trip lines

arcDesigns.combat: Track, flank, cut off and disengage rather than hold formation. Clear pursuit tags to break coordination; keep escort threats readable.

boss.name: The Trailmaster
boss.model: Unique wiry tracker with articulated tracking mantle, asymmetric spool pack and long hooked spear
phases: Tests pursuit with spear feints and marked shots
Deploys destructible tether routes and relocates
Loses tracking assistance; commits to close-range combinations with recovery gaps
boss.counterplay: Read body feints, sever tethers and intercept relocation; no invisible traps or instant off-camera damage

arcDesigns.animation: Low lateral sprint, terrain-aware stop, tether throw/reel, bow brace, stumbling escape and gear-weighted collapse.
arcDesigns.introduction: 21–23 runners/harriers and existing rival groups;24–26 tag and charge mechanics;27–29 route-denial combinations;30 contains only a confrontation compatible with the existing escape toward Shambhala.

arcDesigns.title: Shambhala & Ashwatthama
arcDesigns.faction: Veilbreak Survey — proposed covert sanctuary-hunting expedition
arcDesigns.identity: Seeks routes and signals that expose the hidden refuge; gives the existing scout, river evacuation and beacon missions concrete opposing intent without revealing Ashwatthama's whole past.
arcDesigns.design: Cliff-climbing harnesses, narrow insect-like survey masks, rain capes, jointed climbing frames and low crawling equipment; no hunter wraps or city security bodies.

roster.basic: Rope Pathfinder: climbing axe and short buckler; probes ledges before engaging
roster.elite: Veil Cutter: split climbing staff and retractable wrist guard; parries then retreats toward scouts
roster.heavy: Anchor Bearer: low, broad mechanical climbing frame; plants a shielded observation anchor
roster.ranged: Echo Lancer: elongated acoustic rangefinder and bolt staff; exposes its sightline before firing
roster.special: Beacon Scribe: multi-antenna pack; builds a visible, interruptible signal rather than dealing constant damage

arcDesigns.combat: Search, establish observation and coordinate incursions. Prevent signals and defend evacuation spaces; respect ally roles and the player's agency.

boss.name: The Surveyor
boss.model: Unique articulated cliff frame surrounding an exposed masked navigator; folding survey mast and anchor limbs
phases: Triangulates marked sightlines with reachable anchor nodes
Climbs to authored perches and sends interruptible survey pulses
Damaged mast forces ground combat with long committed staff sweeps
boss.counterplay: Break observation links, use cover and attack exposed recovery windows; place encounter only where the existing perimeter/beacon story supports it

arcDesigns.animation: Harness-supported climb, anchor placement, cautious ledge traversal, signal channel interruption, staff guard break and tether-supported fall.
arcDesigns.introduction: 31 environmental traces and limited scouts;32 preserves the Immortal Stranger introduction;33–36 demonstrate surveying and evacuation pressure;37 preserves the Oath's partial disclosure;38–40 escalate perimeter/signaling opposition.

arcDesigns.title: The Awakening
arcDesigns.faction: Obsidian Breach Corps — proposed specialized Complex siege force
arcDesigns.identity: A distinct assault corps of the established regime, not a replacement for the Complex forces already named in the story.
arcDesigns.design: Low angular basalt-ceramic plating, reinforced triangular helmets, huge shoulder-driven siege rigs and exposed heat-management assemblies. Separate meshes from Directorate logistics units.

roster.basic: Breach Spear: compact armored infantry with folding impact pike; advances under cover
roster.elite: Rift Fencer: segmented arm shield and cleaving saber; stance changes after a readable cue
roster.heavy: Mantlet Walker: six-legged armored siege carriage; exposes cooling joints after firing
roster.ranged: Cinder Mortar: kneeling recoil cradle and arcing launcher; persistent landing indicators
roster.special: Sapper Crucible: low demolition rig; installs interruptible breach charges and withdraws

arcDesigns.combat: Combined-arms siege pressure, cover suppression, breach preparation and safe-lane evacuation. Bound simultaneous area denial so movement/dodge always has counterplay.

boss.name: Breach Regent
boss.model: Unique asymmetric walking siege platform with deployable mantlets and a piloted command core
phases: Mantlet advance creates readable flanking lanes
Anchored artillery exposes coolant joints between salvos
Broken platform fights from one surviving limb with long recovery windows
boss.counterplay: Interrupt salvos, exploit joint exposure and protect evacuation lanes. Do not overwrite the established memory/Karna revelation sequence or invent a replacement final villain

arcDesigns.animation: Pike formation advance, mantlet bracing, heavy recoil, joint-specific stagger, emergency venting and staged mechanical failure.
arcDesigns.introduction: 41–43 assault infantry and sappers;44–45 heavy/mortar combinations tied to escape and last stand;46–49 preserve authored memories/revelations, with distinct memory opposition only if supported by scripts;50 preserves the existing road-beyond purpose.

arcDesigns.title: A New Dawn
arcDesigns.identity: Profits from damaged frontier water infrastructure; opposition must not turn the existing council and clan missions into indiscriminate combat.
arcDesigns.design: Waterproof rubber aprons, pipe-framework armor, exposed scarred faces and barrel-shaped pressure suits.

roster.basic: Valve Thug: pipe club and pressure shove
roster.elite: Lockkeeper: paired valve shields and trapping stance
roster.heavy: Pressure Hauler: round tank suit with slow vented charge
roster.ranged: Jet Gunner: narrow pressure lance with clearly limited reach
roster.special: Tap Saboteur: repairs enemy pressure links; interruptible

arcDesigns.combat: Pressure cycles, supply denial and defensible shutoff valves rather than siege formations.

boss.name: The Reservoir Broker
boss.model: Unique rotary pressure exosuit with offset tank wheel
phases: Controlled jet lanes
Valve network overload
Depleted suit close combat
boss.counterplay: Shut off exposed feeds and exploit depressurization; no required civilian resource destruction

arcDesigns.animation: Valve crank, hose recoil, weighted tank gait, pressure stumble and suit depressurization collapse.
arcDesigns.introduction: Teach one pressure threat early; add support links mid-arc; reserve combinations for existing outer-watch/conflict missions.

arcDesigns.title: The Far Frontier
arcDesigns.faction: Brine Wardens — proposed salt-sea salvage fleet
arcDesigns.identity: Controls access to drowned machinery and tidal routes; supports existing raider and Warden Fleet chapters.
arcDesigns.design: Corroded diving shells, elongated flotation collars, finned salvage frames and netted ballast harnesses.

roster.basic: Salt Boarder: hooked boarding blade and sliding approach
roster.elite: Reef Duelist: articulated harpoon staff and angled deflection
roster.heavy: Ballast Crawler: broad tracked salvage suit; slow anchor sweep
roster.ranged: Line Harpooner: tether launcher with severable line
roster.special: Tide Tender: deploys visible flotation mines and recalls unused devices

arcDesigns.combat: Tidal route timing, pulls, anchored positioning and temporary shoals; no unavoidable drowning traps.

boss.name: Low-Tide Warden
boss.model: Unique broad salvage diving rig with rotating ballast arms
phases: Anchored harpoon duel
Exposed tidal platforms and ballast swings
Drained ballast exposes slow recovery
boss.counterplay: Sever tethers and use marked safe footing; fits A Duel at Low Tide without rewriting its purpose

arcDesigns.animation: Ballast-weighted steps, boarding vaults, harpoon recoil, sliding recovery and pressure-shell collapse.
arcDesigns.introduction: Early boarders, mid-arc fleet support and tide units, then a mechanically earned low-tide confrontation.

arcDesigns.title: The War of Cities
arcDesigns.faction: Banner Compact Legions — proposed hostile city-aligned military coalition
arcDesigns.identity: Disciplined civic armies with rival subgroups; retain the archive's political divisions and alliance choices.
arcDesigns.design: Architectural fan crests, squared lamellar shields, tailored civic uniforms and wheeled pavise frames; distinguish subgroup silhouettes, not only banners/colors.

roster.basic: Rank Soldier: folding shield and thrust blade; maintains formation
roster.elite: Standard Duelist: fan-crest helm and countering poleblade
roster.heavy: Pavise Engine: wheeled deployable shield carriage with crew
roster.ranged: Volley Arbalist: mechanical repeater with synchronized reload
roster.special: Signal Cantor: visible command gestures coordinate one local formation

arcDesigns.combat: Formation cohesion, command interruption and reload exploitation; explicitly different from Arc2's powered shield links.

boss.name: The Iron Envoy
boss.model: Unique armored commander with folding fan shield and long segmented glaive
phases: Formal shield duel
Commanded formations with limited reinforcement budget
Broken shield changes glaive stance
boss.counterplay: Interrupt commands and punish committed guards; preserve any established diplomatic choice instead of forcing a kill

arcDesigns.animation: Formation step, brace, synchronized reload, distinct glaive guards, shield-break stumble and commander collapse.
arcDesigns.introduction: Three Banners establishes groups; siege chapters introduce engines; envoy/council chapters retain diplomatic purpose; later battles combine learned formations.

arcDesigns.title: The Celestial Engine
arcDesigns.faction: Meridian Custodians — proposed ancient autonomous vault defenses
arcDesigns.identity: Protects the engine through protocols rather than human bounty motives; no new mythology revelation imposed on existing scripts.
arcDesigns.design: Non-humanoid stone-metal orbital frames, negative-space torsos, rotating limb rings and lens cores; no human guard reskins.

roster.basic: Arc Strider: three-joint crescent limbs and timed lateral cuts
roster.elite: Parallax Sentinel: split orbiting shield halves; alternates vulnerable plane
roster.heavy: Vault Orrery: slow multi-ring core on radial legs
roster.ranged: Lens Cantilever: fixed beam arm with a visible charging lens
roster.special: Key Lattice: hovering geometry that redirects marked attack paths

arcDesigns.combat: Readable geometric cycles, line redirection and protocol interruption; action remains spatial, not a color-matching gimmick.

boss.name: Axis Keeper
boss.model: Unique nested orrery with independent axial rig and separable ring limbs
phases: One rotating danger plane
Two alternating rings and accessible control nodes
Uncoupled core with patterned openings
boss.counterplay: Read ring orientation and interrupt reachable nodes; keep the Engine story and choices intact

arcDesigns.animation: Authored axial movement, ring arrest, fractured orbit hit reactions, reassembly defense and bounded disassembly death.
arcDesigns.introduction: Early keys teach strider cycles; vault chapters add lenses/lattices; engine chapters combine only previously taught patterns.

arcDesigns.title: The Next Era
arcDesigns.faction: Crown Remnant — proposed adaptive loyalist command
arcDesigns.identity: A distinct successor-era opposition tied to the existing heir/crown chapters; do not predetermine allegiance, the child's fate or final campaign choices.
arcDesigns.design: Faceted open-crown helmets, asymmetrically folded alloy mantles, synthetic tendon frames and tall command units. New meshes, not restored Arc2 or5 armor.

roster.basic: Crown Retainer: folding blade and short controlled burst step
roster.elite: Mirror Adjudicator: stance-reading shield blade with explicitly signaled adaptation
roster.heavy: Throne Carrier: suspended command shell on articulated support limbs
roster.ranged: Halo Fusilier: pivoting shoulder rail with narrow marked salvos
roster.special: Edict Relay: deploys local tactical directives that can be interrupted

arcDesigns.combat: Limited, visible adaptation to repeated tactics; never reads uncommitted player input or permanently disables an ability.

boss.name: Crown Executor — working title
boss.model: Unique segmented mantle rig with independently folding command blades
phases: Establishes one readable directive
Changes between two previously taught stances
Loses relay support and exposes direct-duel recovery
boss.counterplay: Break relays and vary committed tactics; final identity, outcome and placement must follow approved existing story decisions

arcDesigns.animation: Mantle deployment, stance-specific footwork, commanded volleys, interrupted directive recoil and authored multi-stage collapse.
arcDesigns.introduction: Return chapters establish retainers; siege/crown chapters teach directives; final chapters combine known mechanics without replacing narrative resolutions.

acceptanceAndImplementation: Keep Phase2 completion first. This document does not authorize unrelated future gameplay implementation during the open Phase2 cycle.
Before implementation, inspect the then-current mission scripts and align each proposed encounter with its existing purpose; unresolved archive inconsistencies require review, not silent replacement.
Each future arc needs an explicit roster and spawn definition; no automatic previous-arc fallback, reused boss mesh or texture-only replacement.
Review neutral-lit model turnarounds and unlabelled in-game silhouettes for each class and boss. Compare mesh structure, proportions, armor, weapons and locomotion, not just names or palette.

Author appropriate attack, locomotion, defense, hit and death clips; share compatible skeleton infrastructure only when final motion and silhouette remain distinct. Test sockets and collision alignment.
Introduce one mechanic safely, then a support interaction, then combined encounters. Telegraph new boss patterns before tightening their combinations.
Test actual damage windows, dodge/block counterplay, AI decisions, collision, off-camera threats, mission interactions, death/restart and reward persistence in production.

Optimize for integrated GPUs with per-arc streaming, shared materials within each kit, LOD, pooled bounded effects, animation culling and encounter budgets. Unique visuals do not require simultaneously loading all rosters.
Measure frame time, P95, GPU timing, draw calls, geometry and texture memory at matched resolution during dense encounters. Do not claim60FPS until measured.
Complete acceptance requires played production evidence for the new roster and bosses, plus preserved campaign choices and saves. Concepts alone do not satisfy implementation.
